subject.title: Codex-OAuth models fail over incorrectly — sibling model with healthy per-model quota still drops to non-codex fallback

question: For Codex OAuth sibling-model failover, should OpenClaw keep Codex models on the app-server and pursue the suspected upstream WebSocket/rate-limit issue, or should it add direct-runtime Codex Harmony tool-call support as a supported fallback path?
rationale: Both directions can plausibly address parts of the report, but the choice changes provider routing, app-server ownership, and tool-call parsing behavior, so automation should not pick it without maintainer intent and live Codex proof.

options.title: Finish app-server path first
options.body: Keep the app-server as the default Codex runtime, review the model-scoped bookkeeping PR, and require live evidence before changing upstream WebSocket behavior.

options.title: Add direct Harmony support
options.body: Implement a bounded Harmony tool-call adapter for direct OpenAI Responses and prove Codex tool calls work before considering direct Codex routing.

options.title: Defer pending stronger proof
options.body: Keep the issue open for a maintainer-owned live repro that distinguishes local cooldown skip from upstream app-server false-429 behavior.

recommendation.title: Finish app-server path first
recommendation.body: Keep the app-server as the default Codex runtime, review the model-scoped bookkeeping PR, and require live evidence before changing upstream WebSocket behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available routing owner from Codex harness/provider history and were explicitly mentioned in the issue discussion for this decision.
